gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Victron MultiPlus-II 48/5000/70-50, which the StoryOfSolar ranking names, puts out 230 VAC at 50 Hz with no UL listing. A US off-grid home needs Victron's separate 120 V line, whose 48 V units are UL 1741-listed and give 120 VAC at 60 Hz (the 48/3000/35-50 gives 2,400 W).
standout_why: I compared five pages. The EG4 6000XP product page (the one ChatGPT cited) says its closed-loop link works with 'EG4 48V batteries' and points to a compatibility-list PDF without naming any other brands. The Signature Solar 6000XP page says the same. WildJoule lists Victron 'MultiPlus-II 48/5000' with no region or voltage variant and has no battery-communication detail. StoryOfSolar ranks the 'Victron MultiPlus-II 48/5000/70-50' at #2 without saying it is a 230 V / 50 Hz model. None of them gives a model-by-region match for Victron. None says which Victron 48 V models are UL 1741-listed, and none notes that one 48/3000 variant is not.
decides: For a US off-grid shopper this rules out the Victron model one top-ranked page recommends. If the shopper wants Victron, the choice is the 120 V line, 48/3000/35-50 (UL 1741, 2,400 W) or 48/5000/70-95 (UL 1741 + UL 458). That makes Victron a multi-unit build plus a separate MPPT charge controller to reach 120/240 V. The single-box 120/240 V options are the EG4 6000XP and the Sun Gold Power SPH6548P, which is cheaper and which Dealectric already lists. The SPH6548P accepts 550 Voc against the 6000XP's 480 V. It also runs with lead-acid batteries or with no battery at all, and parallels to 6 units.
